title: Pediatric Appendicitis Score (PAS)
sources: Critical Vector — Pediatric Appendicitis: Three Scores, One Diagnosis (Alvarado vs PAS vs pARC)
Kharbanda AB et al. pARC derivation/validation. Pediatrics 2018;141(4):e20172699
Cotton DM et al. pARC community-ED validation. Ann Emerg Med 2019;74(4):471-480

changelog.change: Added the three-score comparison (Alvarado / PAS / pARC), the head-to-head AUC + decisiveness data (49% vs 23%), and sharpened per-tool pitfalls from the CV audit.
Initial entry — PAS filed in Peds Module nav per Peds_Module_Content_Spec.md.

purpose: Fast ED risk stratification for appendicitis in children when clinical suspicion is already present. A LOW score does not reliably rule appendicitis out — do not treat it as reassurance.

body.text: Three scores, three jobs — not interchangeable

rows: 8 items, 0–10 points (adult-derived, applied to kids by convention)
Low-tech primary-care / outpatient settings with limited labs
Fast ED confirmation when clinical suspicion is already high
7-variable logistic regression → continuous % risk (NOT a point score)
The most individualized estimate; best for guiding the actual imaging decision in kids ≥ 5

body.text: pARC's variables: sex, age, duration of pain, guarding, pain migration, maximal RLQ tenderness, and absolute neutrophil count (ANC) — ANC specifically, which is what separates it from both Alvarado and PAS.

The number to remember: 49% vs 23%. In the pARC validation cohort, pARC confidently classified nearly half of patients into a clearly low-risk (< 15%) or clearly high-risk (≥ 85%) category — where clinicians can act on the number directly. A comparably confident PAS cutoff (< 3 or > 8) captured only 23%. pARC's advantage is even larger in real-world community-ED data than in the original derivation.

items: Alvarado: heavily weighted toward WBC (nonspecific) — over-diagnoses in non-appendiceal inflammatory conditions. More accurate at the score extremes than in the equivocal mid-range.

PAS: a score < 4 does NOT reliably exclude appendicitis — do not treat it as reassurance. The cough/hop/percussion item is unreliable in young or uncooperative children. Not a sole decision tool in known GI disease, pregnancy, or prior abdominal surgery.

pARC: validated only in children ≥ 5 y with < 96 h of pain — below that age appendicitis is rare and atypical, and the tool isn't built for it. Requires ANC as an input, not available at every point of care.
